idle-1.note: Gangway adds no listener, socket or timer until a consumer asks for it (the Deck Terminal is M5b), so the app-level scenario is the P1 one plus the lazy host object and one observation of the app lock. cpuAvgPct 0.067 vs P1 0.053 and cpuMaxSamplePct 0.4 vs 0.3 are one top sample (top reports 0.1 steps) on a Mac that other workers were building on (1-minute load 1.9 at the end, 2.6 at the start); wakeups 0.003/s and footprint 81 MB (P1 77 MB) are within noise and every budget is met. threads +1 over baseline: the app's own, fds equal.
idle-1.rerunAfterMergeNote: A second idle-1 run after merging M8b and switching Gangway to TLS (1-minute load 12.6 at its start, above the 8 limit, so it is not recorded): cpu 0.053 %, wakeups 0.007/s, footprint 102 MB first sample and 86 MB last (P1 77 MB, M8b's own merge adds code and stores). Gangway is not started in that scenario, so none of it is Gangway; rerun when the machine is quiet.

environment.cluster: test cluster (minikube), live; kubectl v1.30.14 to v1.37.2

gangway.proxyOverheadNote: Re-measured over TLS (400 sequential GETs of a ConfigMap on one keep-alive connection to the real API server): 0.10 ms p50, 0.12 ms p95 for the proxy's own work; 0.77 ms p50 end to end (1.3 ms in a second run on a loaded machine).

idleWakeups.note: proc_pid_rusage interrupt and package-idle wakeups of the test process over 8 s, with 4 sessions each holding an open keep-alive connection: one single-shot 120 s deadline per connection, no repeating timers.

declinedExecSheets.note: kubectl retries a refused WebSocket upgrade over SPDY; a declined stream is remembered for 3 s.

gangway.transport: HTTP/1.1 over TLS 1.3 on loopback (per-launch in-memory P-256 key, self-signed certificate in the session kubeconfig)

newConnectionPlusFirstRequestMs.note: 60 new TLS connections each with one GET through Gangway to a local fake upstream; a request on an open connection is unaffected.
